answer_summary: Complex 5 is the dinuclear mu-dinitrogen complex [(PNP)Mo]2(mu-N2): a single N2 molecule bridges two (PNP)Mo fragments end-on (mu-eta1:eta1), giving a near-linear Mo-N-N-Mo axis. The gas-uptake data give n(N2)/n(4) = (1.0 bar*94.97 cm3 / R*273.15 K) / (1.00 g/597.824 g/mol) = 2.500 = 5/2, i.e. 1 N2 per 2 Mo. Na-Hg (3 equiv) reduces Mo(III) in (PNP)MoCl3 to Mo(0); the tridentate meridional PNP pincer is retained on each Mo. Drawn with the simplified arc ligand glyph as in 4.
assumptions: Ideal-gas behaviour pV = nRT for N2 (trusted general law).
Half-quantum measurement convention for the printed input quantities (matches IChO2026Chem.Reporting).
Stoichiometric (1:1 Mo:ligand) pincer complex 4 and its retention in 5, as depicted by the unchanged simplified-ligand glyph in the scheme.
3 equiv Na-Hg delivers 3 electrons per Mo (Mo(III) -> Mo(0)); N2 retained as an intact bridge (mild reductant).
source_gaps: The precise N-N bond order in the drawn mu-N2 bridge is a drawing convention; the problem only requires the connectivity (one N2 bridging two Mo). No template fields exist on the blank answer sheet A7-4.
